chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: Drummers catching brass licks
summary: The practice of drums accenting horn licks arose from Chick Webb and Benny Goodman arrangers; Saunders did it from show work, as did Sid Catlett and Jo Jones.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah, well, it wasn't always that way. In the earlier days, say, in the '30s, the rhythm section was more of a section and just sort of kept the pulse.
MR. SAUNDERS: Right.
How did that change? Now, the drummers catch brass licks and thing like that.
Right, well, --
When did that start coming in?

Well, all of this started coming in, I guess, maybe you could say from the time of the Chick Webb band into the Benny Goodman band and things like that. I think it's that late that this would come in. See, and the reason that is, is because the arrangements changed. And the arrangers changed, and the arrangers wanted certain effects and things like that.
And then all of these licks, they wanted these licks heard -- I mean, accentuated.
Yeah.
In other words, it was a brass lick, they wanted it accentuated. And to really accentuate it, the drums would come in with it. Yeah, see, they would do that. That's how that --
So you say around the early '40s?
Yeah, right, well, in --
In the '40s;
Yeah, right, right, right, right, right.
Well, how --
Late '30s, you know.
How did you play, if you can recall, when you first started playing for the big band?

See, I was a combination drummer. I did the shows, and then I had to do one thing with them, and then it made it easier for me playing in the big bands, because with the dances and all these type things, you caught the little cute things that they were doing, and different things like that.
So then it just spills over into the band. And when you do that, then you get the little cute things that they're playing in the horns.
That makes sense.
Right, uh-huh, right.
So you always were catching things in the band?
Yeah, right, right, right. Yeah.
That was -- you were one of the first to do that, I guess.
Well, it was -- well, Sid would do those things. Big Sid would do those things.
With Louis' band.
With Louis' band and things like that, because he was -- and then he played with Benny's band.
Right.

And things like that. And he was doing all of those things then. Because he was -- they would call them cute drummers, at that time. He's a cute drummer, he's playing them little cute things. Right, then later Jo came along and he was doing it.
Right. Well, he started using some accents with the bass drum.
Yeah, right, right, right.
